# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

This report selects and **fully specifies** the five models that agents a05–a09 will implement and
a11–a15 will calibrate. It is written so that a builder can code its slot from
`config/models.yaml` plus the corresponding section here *without reading any other document*.

Three requirements drive every choice:

1. **Maximise the chance of the best possible reproduction of daily $Q$.** Independent benchmarks *at this
   exact gauge* (USGS 02472000) put calibrated conceptual models at NSE 0.69–0.82 (SAC-SMA 0.796,
   HBV 0.819, FUSE 0.775–0.779, VIC 0.72, mHM 0.70) and regional LSTMs at NSE 0.84–0.86 [@kratzert2019].
   Our target band is therefore **NSE 0.80–0.87 on calibration and 0.74–0.85 on evaluation**.
2. **Span a complexity gradient** so that the study can answer *does complexity pay off?*
3. **Be complementary**, because a16 also evaluates the ensembles pre-declared in
   `config/models.yaml → ensembles:` (@sec-ensembles).

Everything below is constrained by CLAUDE.md rule 3: **no statistic of observed $Q$ inside
1948-10-01…1951-09-30 may influence any model choice, feature, bound or scaling constant.**
All numbers quoted from data in this report come from the *calibration* window only.

::: {.callout-important}
## Two slow stores, not one
a01 reports a master-recession residence time of 9–11 d while the GAGES-II subsurface *contact time* is
549 d, and a02 finds a Brutsaert–Nieber exponent $b = 1.68 \ne 1$. A single linear groundwater reservoir
cannot reconcile those two numbers. Every conceptual slot below therefore contains **either** a non-linear
storage–discharge relation (GR4J routing store, $Q \propto R^5$) **or** two lower-zone outlets with
different time constants (HBV `SUZ`/`SLZ`, SAC-SMA `LZFSC`/`LZFPC`). This is the single most important
structural conclusion of @sec-evidence.
:::

# Selection method {#sec-selection}

## Criteria and weights

Each candidate is scored 1–5 (5 = best) on seven criteria; the weighted total drives the portfolio.
Weights reflect the project objective ("best reproduction of daily streamflow", KGE/NSE on a 1003-day
window) and the hard laptop compute budget (≤ 3 h per optimizer, $10^4$–$10^5$ model runs).

## Why these five, and what was rejected {#sec-why}

**Selected:** ARX–API ridge (slot 1), GR4J (2), HBV-light without snow (3), SAC-SMA without Snow-17 (4),
single-basin LSTM (5).

The screening is **not** a pure ranking exercise: slot 1 is included *by design* even though HYMOD
scores marginally higher (3.90 vs 3.84). A statistical lower benchmark is mandatory for the project's
central question ("does complexity pay off?") — without it the gradient has no origin — and its low
process score is precisely the point. Everything above slot 1 in the screening that is *not* selected is
rejected for the reasons below.

Rejections and overrides, with reasons:

* **HYMOD is not used, although it is the historical Leaf River model** [@boyle2001; @vrugt2003].
  The skill's default set proposes it; I override it and log the decision. HYMOD routes its slow response
  through a *single linear* reservoir, which is exactly the structure a02 falsifies
  ($b = 1.68 \ne 1$, and 9-d vs 549-d time scales). Its production store is a Moore PDM
  [@moore1985], i.e. conceptually the same variable-contributing-area idea already carried by GR4J's
  production store and HBV's $\beta$ function, so it would add little complementarity at 5 parameters —
  a slot almost identical in complexity to GR4J's 4. Replacing it with **HBV-light** buys (i) an explicit
  threshold `UZL` in the fast response, (ii) two subsurface time scales, (iii) the best documented
  at-gauge conceptual score (NSE 0.819, a01), and (iv) it fills the complexity gap between 4 and 15
  parameters. The historical Leaf River lineage is preserved through SAC-SMA, which is the model of
  @duan1992, @sorooshian1993 and @boyle2001 on this very record.
* **TOPMODEL** requires a topographic-index distribution; a01 only provides a single GAGES-II TWI value
  (12.69), so the index histogram would have to be invented. Rejected on data demands.
* **Xinanjiang / PDM / FUSE / MARRMoT** score well on process but add nothing that SAC-SMA + HBV do not
  already cover, and FUSE/MARRMoT would mean porting a framework (high implementation risk in one session).
* **Gradient boosting / GRU / TCN**: a tree ensemble cannot carry state, so it needs the same hand-made
  antecedent features as slot 1 while losing the closed-form transparency; GRU/TCN are near-duplicates of
  the LSTM with less hydrological literature. Rejected on complementarity.
* **dPL / differentiable hybrid** [@feng2022] scores highest on process and complementarity but has the
  worst implementation risk (a torch time-stepping loop with smoothed thresholds, trained jointly with a
  network, written blind by one agent in one session) and the worst compute score. **The hybrid idea is
  not lost**: it re-enters as the pre-declared ensembles `ens_physics_plus_ml` and
  `ens_best_conceptual_plus_lstm` (@sec-ensembles), which a16 evaluates with weights fixed on
  calibration data only — the same scientific question at a fraction of the risk.

The LSTM count is $4H(n_{\text{in}}+H) + 4H + (H+1)$ weights with $H = 64$, $n_{\text{in}} = 14$:
**`{python} int(4*64*(14+64) + 4*64 + 65)`** trainable weights against 10,592 training days — roughly
**1.9 weights per training day**, which is why heavy regularisation (dropout 0.4, early stopping,
5-seed averaging) is prescribed in @sec-model5.

# Slot 1 — ARX–API ridge regression {#sec-model1}

## Overview

A **persistence-free linear model**: the predictors are non-linear functions of the *forcing only*
($P$, $PET$, day of year); no observed or simulated $Q$ enters the right-hand side, so the comparison with
the conceptual slots is fair (a catchment model also only sees $P$ and $PET$). The two ideas that lift it
above a naive regression are (i) **antecedent precipitation indices** (API), the oldest storage proxy in
hydrology and the backbone of IHACRES-type models [@jakeman1993], and (ii) a **Box–Cox target transform**
[@box1964] with a bias-corrected back-transform [@duan1983], which handles the extreme skew of daily $Q$
(a02: skew 6.85). Estimation is ridge regression [@hoerl1970], i.e. closed form, so one model evaluation
costs one $\sim 22 \times 22$ linear solve.

**Why for the Leaf River.** a02 shows that the $R^2$ of a linear model on lagged $P$ rises monotonically
with the lag window (0.59 at 10 d → 0.65 at 365 d): most of the daily signal *is* input memory. This slot
quantifies exactly how much, and thereby prices the conceptual structure of slots 2–4.

## Conceptual diagram

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  P[P_t] --> L["lagged rain<br/>P_t .. P_t-n"]
  P --> AF["A_fast = λf·A + P"]
  P --> AM["A_med = λm·A + P"]
  P --> AS["A_slow = λs·A + P"]
  E[PET_t] --> EA["E_ant = λe·E + PET"]
  D[day of year] --> H["4 harmonics"]
  L --> X[["design matrix Z<br/>(standardised)"]]
  AF --> X
  AM --> X
  AS --> X
  EA --> X
  H --> X
  AM -.->|"interaction P·A"| X
  X --> R["ridge<br/>β = (ZᵀZ+αnI')⁻¹Zᵀy"]
  R --> Y["ŷ = Zβ (Box-Cox space)"]
  Y --> B["inverse Box-Cox<br/>× bias factor c"]
  B --> Q[["Q̂_t (mm/d)"]]
```

## Perceptual → conceptual assumptions

*Represented*: catchment wetness memory at three time scales; a variable runoff coefficient through the
$P_t \times A_t$ interaction terms; the drying effect of accumulated PET; residual seasonality.
*Ignored*: mass conservation (nothing forces $\sum \hat Q \le \sum P$ except the bias factor), explicit
states, threshold behaviour beyond the quadratic/interaction terms, and any non-stationarity.

## Mathematical formulation

Recursive feature states, computed forward over the contiguous forcing frame with zero initial values:

$$A^{(j)}_t = \lambda_j\,A^{(j)}_{t-1} + P_t,\qquad j \in \{\text{fast},\text{med},\text{slow}\},\qquad A^{(j)}_{-1}=0
$$ {#eq-api}

$$E^{\text{ant}}_t = \lambda_e\,E^{\text{ant}}_{t-1} + \mathrm{PET}_t,\qquad E^{\text{ant}}_{-1}=0
$$ {#eq-eant}

The effective memory of @eq-api is $1/(1-\lambda_j)$ days, hence the bounds in @tbl-p1
(1.4–5 d, 5–20 d, 20–1000 d), which bracket the a02 response lag (1–3 d), recession time (9.1 d) and the
GAGES-II contact time (549 d).

Design row (with $n_\ell = $ `n_lag`, $d_t$ = day of year, $\omega = 2\pi/365.25$):

$$
\mathbf{z}_t = \Big[\,1,\;
P_t,\dots,P_{t-n_\ell},\;
A^{(f)}_t, A^{(m)}_t, A^{(s)}_t,\;
E^{\text{ant}}_t,\;
\sqrt{P_t},\;
\tfrac{P_t A^{(m)}_t}{100},\;
\tfrac{P_t A^{(s)}_t}{100},\;
\big(\tfrac{A^{(s)}_t}{100}\big)^2,\;
\sin\omega d_t,\cos\omega d_t,\sin 2\omega d_t,\cos 2\omega d_t \,\Big]
$$ {#eq-design}

With $n_\ell = 5$ that is 21 columns including the intercept. Target transform (Box–Cox):

$$
y_t = g(Q_t;\lambda_{bc}) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{Q_t^{\lambda_{bc}} - 1}{\lambda_{bc}}, & \lambda_{bc} > 10^{-6}\\[4pt]
\ln Q_t, & \text{otherwise,}\end{cases}
\qquad
g^{-1}(y) = \begin{cases}\big(\max(\lambda_{bc} y + 1,\,10^{-9})\big)^{1/\lambda_{bc}}\\ e^{y}\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-boxcox}

($Q>0$ always, a02, so no offset is needed.) Columns 2… of $Z$ are standardised with the **fitting-window**
mean and standard deviation; the intercept column is left alone and is not penalised:

$$\hat{\boldsymbol\beta} = \big(Z^\top Z + \alpha\,n\,I'\big)^{-1} Z^\top \mathbf{y},
\qquad \alpha = 10^{\texttt{log10\_ridge\_alpha}},\quad I'=\mathrm{diag}(0,1,\dots,1)
$$ {#eq-ridge}

Output equation, with the multiplicative bias correction $c$ estimated on the fitting window only:

$$\hat Q_t = c\cdot\max\!\big(g^{-1}(\mathbf{z}_t^\top\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}),\,0.05\big),
\qquad c = \frac{\sum_{t\in\text{fit}} Q_t}{\sum_{t\in\text{fit}}\max(g^{-1}(\mathbf{z}_t^\top\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}),0.05)}
$$ {#eq-out1}

## Parameters

```{python}
#| label: tbl-p1
#| tbl-cap: "Slot 1 hyperparameters (the 21 regression coefficients are fitted in closed form and are not searched)."
def ptab(slot):
    m = [x for x in MODELS["models"] if x["slot"] == slot][0]
    d = pd.DataFrame(m["parameters"])
    keep = [c for c in ["name", "units", "lower", "upper", "default", "integer", "description", "source"] if c in d]
    return d[keep]
ptab(1)
```

## Initial states and warm-up

$A^{(j)}_{-1}=E^{\text{ant}}_{-1}=0$. With $\lambda_{\text{slow}} \le 0.999$ the slowest recursion needs
$\approx 3/(1-\lambda) \approx 3000$ d to be fully spun up in the worst case, but $\ge 365$ d removes >97 %
of the transient for $\lambda \le 0.992$; `warmup_days_min: 365` is declared, and a11 must keep
$\lambda_{\text{slow}} \le 0.995$ if the evaluation warm-up (92 d) is a concern — the model is
*standardised*, so a residual spin-up offset is largely absorbed by the intercept.

## Mass balance check

Not applicable (no stores). The builder must instead assert, on the fitting window,
$0.9 \le \overline{\hat Q}/\overline{Q} \le 1.1$ (guaranteed by @eq-out1 up to the clipping) and
$\hat Q_t > 0\;\forall t$.

## Numerical pitfalls

* Standardise the design columns *before* the ridge solve, otherwise $\alpha$ means something different for
  every column; store the means/sds in the artefact and reuse them at prediction time.
* Use `scipy.linalg.solve(A, b, assume_a="pos")`, never `np.linalg.inv`.
* Clip $\lambda_{bc}y+1$ at $10^{-9}$ before the fractional power (@eq-boxcox), otherwise NaNs appear for
  strongly negative predictions.
* `n_lag` arrives from a continuous optimizer: round it (`int(round(x))`) and clip to [1, 10].
* The first `n_lag` rows of the frame have undefined lags: fill with 0 (dry) and exclude them from fitting.

## Implementation route

From scratch, `numpy` + `scipy.linalg`. `kind: "trainable"`, so:
`fit(forcing, target, params)` builds @eq-design, solves @eq-ridge and stores
$(\hat\beta, \text{col means/sds}, c, \lambda_{bc}, n_\ell)$; `simulate(forcing, params)` rebuilds the
features on the frame it is given and applies the stored coefficients.
**Lazy-fit rule:** if `simulate` is called on an unfitted instance it must fit itself on the calibration
window obtained through `src.common.data` (never `slice_run(..., "evaluation")`) and emit a warning.
`save`/`load` must round-trip a plain `.npz`/`.json` artefact.

Fitting protocol (also in `config/models.yaml → fit_protocol`): coefficients on
`calibration_internal.train`, hyperparameters selected on `calibration_internal.validation`, then a final
closed-form **refit of the coefficients on the full calibration metric window** with the selected
hyperparameters. No evaluation data at any stage.

## Expected behaviour

Strengths: unbiased in the mean by construction, extremely cheap, no equifinality drama, and a
transparent statement of "how much is memory". Weaknesses: no mass conservation, it will smear flood
peaks (a linear map cannot produce a 45 mm/d spike from a 100 mm storm on dry soil), and recessions decay
as a mixture of exponentials fixed by $\lambda_j$ rather than by storage. **Expected NSE 0.60–0.75
(calibration), 0.50–0.72 (evaluation)**; KGE $\alpha$ clearly below 1 (variance under-dispersion).

# Slot 2 — GR4J {#sec-model2}

## Overview

GR4J [@perrin2003] is the four-parameter daily lumped model of the French "Génie Rural" family, developed
by successive structural simplification tested on 429 catchments. It is the standard parsimony benchmark
in comparative hydrology and is available as the R package `airGR` [@coron2017], which the builder should
use as a numerical **test oracle** if R is available (it is not required). @wang2024 applied GR-type and
other lumped structures to this very record.

**Why for the Leaf River.** GR4J satisfies four of the five hard requirements with four parameters:
a soil-moisture-dependent production function (variable runoff coefficient), ET that can reach PET, a
**non-linear routing store** with $Q_r \propto R^5$ for small $R$ — the direct analogue of the observed
Brutsaert–Nieber $b = 1.68$ — and a 1–3 d unit hydrograph. Its weak point here is that it has *one* slow
store; the exchange term $x_2$ then has to absorb the long-term balance, which makes it an interesting
diagnostic (a01 flags inter-catchment exchange as a MEDIUM-priority process).

## Conceptual diagram

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  P[P] --> N{"P ≥ E ?"}
  E[E = PET] --> N
  N -->|yes| PN["Pn = P − E, En = 0"]
  N -->|no| EN["En = E − P, Pn = 0"]
  PN --> PS["Ps (eq. 2.2)"]
  EN --> ES["Es (eq. 2.3)"]
  PS --> S[("production store S<br/>capacity x1")]
  ES -.-> S
  S --> PERC["Perc (eq. 2.5)"]
  PN --> DIR["Pn − Ps"]
  PERC --> PR["Pr = Perc + (Pn − Ps)"]
  DIR --> PR
  PR --> U1["0.9·Pr → UH1 (base x4)"]
  PR --> U2["0.1·Pr → UH2 (base 2x4)"]
  U1 --> Q9["Q9"]
  U2 --> Q1["Q1"]
  Q9 --> R[("routing store R<br/>ref. capacity x3")]
  F["exchange F = x2·(R/x3)^3.5"] --> R
  F --> QD
  R --> QR["Qr = R·(1−(1+(R/x3)^4)^(−1/4))"]
  Q1 --> QD["Qd = max(0, Q1 + F)"]
  QR --> Q[["Q = Qr + Qd"]]
  QD --> Q
```

## Perceptual → conceptual assumptions

*Represented*: soil-moisture control of the runoff coefficient (saturation-excess in a bulk sense),
ET limited by soil water, percolation to a routing store, non-linear release, translation delay, and a
net gain/loss of groundwater across the topographic divide.
*Ignored*: separate tension/free water, an explicit second (very slow) aquifer, any snow or frozen ground,
and a distinction between fast surface and fast subsurface flow.

## Mathematical formulation

State variables: $S$ (production store, mm, $0\le S\le x_1$), $R$ (routing store, mm, $R\ge 0$), plus the
two unit-hydrograph memory vectors. Order of operations within day $t$ (explicit, operator-split; this is
the scheme actually used, not an ODE solver):

**(1) Net forcing.** With $E = \mathrm{PET}_t$:
$$P_n = \max(P_t - E,\,0),\qquad E_n = \max(E - P_t,\,0) \quad(\text{only one is non-zero})$$ {#eq-gr1}

**(2) Rain entering the production store.**
$$P_s = \frac{x_1\left(1-\left(\frac{S}{x_1}\right)^2\right)\tanh\!\frac{P_n}{x_1}}
{1+\frac{S}{x_1}\tanh\!\frac{P_n}{x_1}}$$ {#eq-gr2}

**(3) Actual evaporation from the store.**
$$E_s = \frac{S\left(2-\frac{S}{x_1}\right)\tanh\!\frac{E_n}{x_1}}
{1+\left(1-\frac{S}{x_1}\right)\tanh\!\frac{E_n}{x_1}}$$ {#eq-gr3}

**(4) Store update.** $\;S \leftarrow S - E_s + P_s$.

**(5) Percolation.**
$$\mathrm{Perc} = S\left[1-\left(1+\left(\tfrac{4}{9}\tfrac{S}{x_1}\right)^{4}\right)^{-1/4}\right],
\qquad S \leftarrow S - \mathrm{Perc}$$ {#eq-gr5}

**(6) Routed volume.** $\;P_r = \mathrm{Perc} + (P_n - P_s)$, split 90 % / 10 %.

**(7) Unit hydrographs.** With $\mathrm{SH}_1(u)=0$ for $u\le0$, $(u/x_4)^{5/2}$ for $0<u<x_4$, $1$ for
$u\ge x_4$; and $\mathrm{SH}_2(u)= \tfrac12 (u/x_4)^{5/2}$ for $0<u<x_4$,
$1-\tfrac12(2-u/x_4)^{5/2}$ for $x_4\le u<2x_4$, $1$ for $u\ge 2x_4$:
$$u^{(1)}_j = \mathrm{SH}_1(j)-\mathrm{SH}_1(j-1),\quad j=1..\lceil x_4\rceil;\qquad
u^{(2)}_j = \mathrm{SH}_2(j)-\mathrm{SH}_2(j-1),\quad j=1..\lceil 2x_4\rceil$$ {#eq-gr7}
$$Q_9 = 0.9\sum_j u^{(1)}_j P_r(t-j+1),\qquad Q_1 = 0.1\sum_j u^{(2)}_j P_r(t-j+1)$$ {#eq-gr8}

**(8) Groundwater exchange.** $\;F = x_2\left(\dfrac{R}{x_3}\right)^{7/2}$

**(9) Routing store.** $\;R \leftarrow \max(0,\;R + Q_9 + F)$, then
$$Q_r = R\left[1-\left(1+\left(\tfrac{R}{x_3}\right)^{4}\right)^{-1/4}\right],\qquad R \leftarrow R - Q_r$$ {#eq-gr9}

**(10) Output.** $\;Q_d = \max(0,\,Q_1+F)$, $\;\boxed{Q_t = Q_r + Q_d}$

For small $R/x_3$, @eq-gr9 expands to $Q_r \approx R^5/(4x_3^4)$: a strongly non-linear storage–discharge
relation, which is precisely why GR4J can reproduce a $b>1$ recession with a single store.

## Parameters

```{python}
#| label: tbl-p2
#| tbl-cap: "Slot 2 (GR4J) parameters. Bounds combine Perrin et al. (2003) with the a01 physical priors."
ptab(2)
```

## Initial states and warm-up

$S_0 = 0.30\,x_1$, $R_0 = 0.50\,x_3$, both UH memories zero (airGR convention). These depend only on
parameters, never on observations, so they are legitimate in the evaluation window.
`warmup_days_min: 365`.

## Mass balance check (builder must test)

Accumulating over any window,
$$\sum P - \sum E_s - \sum Q \;+\; \sum F^{\text{added}} \;=\; \Delta S + \Delta R + \Delta \mathrm{UH}_1 + \Delta \mathrm{UH}_2$$ {#eq-gr-mb}
where $F^{\text{added}}$ is the exchange water actually added (i.e. after the $\max(0,\cdot)$ clips in
steps 9 and 10, counted once for the routing branch and once for the direct branch). Required tolerance:
$|\text{residual}| < 10^{-8}$ mm per 1000 days. Run the test with $x_2=0$ first (then $F\equiv0$ and the
identity is exact), then with $x_2=\pm3$ mm/d.

## Numerical pitfalls

* $\tanh$ overflows for arguments $\gtrsim 20$; clip $P_n/x_1$ and $E_n/x_1$ at 13.
* $\sum_j u^{(1)}_j = \sum_j u^{(2)}_j = 1$ must hold to $10^{-12}$; recompute ordinates whenever $x_4$
  changes (i.e. once per parameter set, not per time step).
* $\lceil x_4\rceil$ with $x_4 = 1.0$ gives a single ordinate — make sure the array is never empty
  (bounds start at 0.5, so $\lceil x_4\rceil\ge1$ always).
* With $x_2<0$ the routing store can be driven negative: clip and *record* the clipped amount for
  @eq-gr-mb.
* Keep $S$ inside $[0,x_1]$ by construction (@eq-gr2–@eq-gr3 guarantee it analytically); add an assertion
  rather than a clip, so a coding error is caught instead of hidden.

## Implementation route

From scratch, NumPy with an explicit daily loop (optionally `numba.njit`); ~40 lines. Follow
@perrin2003 Appendix and the `airGR::RunModel_GR4J` reference [@coron2017]. Validate on
(i) the mass balance above, (ii) a 1-day impulse: a single 100 mm rain on a dry store must produce a
hydrograph whose peak is at day $\approx x_4$ and whose volume equals the routed volume, and (iii) if R is
available, `airGR` output agreement to $10^{-6}$ mm/d.

## Expected behaviour

Strengths: robust, few parameters, very fast ($10^5$ runs are cheap), non-linear recession, excellent
prior evidence on humid catchments. Weaknesses: a single slow store must serve both the 10-d and the
several-hundred-day time scale, so expect systematic under-estimation of very long summer recessions;
$x_2$ may compensate a structural ET error and end up physically implausible (watch $|x_2|>3$ mm/d).
**Expected NSE 0.78–0.86 (calibration), 0.72–0.84 (evaluation).**

# Slot 3 — HBV-light without snow {#sec-model3}

## Overview

HBV [@bergstrom1992; @lindstrom1997] in the "HBV-light" formulation of @seibert2012, with the snow routine
removed (a01 decision: snow = 0.8 % of $P$; DECISIONS.md). Nine parameters: three for the soil routine,
five for the response routine, one for routing. HBV is the best-performing conceptual model documented at
this gauge (calibrated NSE 0.819; uncalibrated 0.687 — a01, after @kratzert2019).

**Why for the Leaf River.** It is the only structure in the portfolio with an **explicit storage threshold**
in the fast response: the outlet $K_0$ only operates when $S_{UZ} > UZL$. a02's event analysis (runoff
coefficients spanning two orders of magnitude and correlated with antecedent wetness, $r = 0.57$) is
exactly the signature of a threshold. It also carries the **two subsurface time scales** demanded by
@sec-evidence ($K_1 \approx 0.1$ d⁻¹ ⇒ $\tau \approx 10$ d; $K_2 \approx 0.002$ d⁻¹ ⇒ $\tau \approx 500$ d),
and its $\beta$-function recharge is a different parameterisation of the variable contributing area than
GR4J's $\tanh$ production store — good for ensemble diversity.

## Conceptual diagram

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  P[P] --> REC["recharge R = P·(SM/FC)^β"]
  P --> SMIN["P − R"]
  SMIN --> SM[("soil moisture SM<br/>capacity FC")]
  PET[PET] --> EA["Ea = PET·min(SM/(LP·FC), 1)"]
  SM --> EA
  EA -->|"to atmosphere"| ATM(("ET"))
  REC --> SUZ[("upper box SUZ")]
  SUZ --> Q0["Q0 = K0·max(SUZ − UZL, 0)"]
  SUZ --> Q1["Q1 = K1·SUZ"]
  SUZ --> PERCF["PERC = min(PERCmax, SUZ)"]
  PERCF --> SLZ[("lower box SLZ")]
  SLZ --> Q2["Q2 = K2·SLZ"]
  Q0 --> SUM["Qgen = Q0+Q1+Q2"]
  Q1 --> SUM
  Q2 --> SUM
  SUM --> UH["triangular UH, base MAXBAS"]
  UH --> Q[["Q (mm/d)"]]
```

## Perceptual → conceptual assumptions

*Represented*: a non-linear (power-law) partition of rain between soil storage and recharge; ET throttled
below a soil-moisture threshold $LP\cdot FC$; a capped percolation to a deep store; a threshold-activated
near-surface outlet, an interflow outlet and a slow baseflow outlet; translation by a symmetric triangle.
*Ignored*: tension/free-water distinction, capillary rise (the optional HBV `CFLUX` term is dropped),
groundwater exchange across the divide, and any land-cover zonation (the basin is run as one lumped zone).

## Mathematical formulation

States: $SM$ (mm, $0\le SM\le FC$), $S_{UZ}$ (mm), $S_{LZ}$ (mm), and the MAXBAS memory.
Order of operations within day $t$ (explicit Euler / operator splitting):

**(1) Recharge (soil routine).**
$$R_t = P_t\left(\frac{SM_{t-1}}{FC}\right)^{\beta},\qquad SM^{*} = SM_{t-1} + P_t - R_t$$ {#eq-hbv1}
If $SM^{*} > FC$, move the excess to recharge: $R_t \leftarrow R_t + (SM^{*}-FC)$, $SM^{*} \leftarrow FC$.

**(2) Actual evaporation.**
$$E_{a,t} = \mathrm{PET}_t \cdot \min\!\left(\frac{SM^{*}}{LP\cdot FC},\,1\right),\qquad
SM_t = \max\!\big(SM^{*} - E_{a,t},\,0\big)$$ {#eq-hbv2}
(if the $\max$ clips, reduce $E_{a,t}$ by the clipped amount so mass is conserved).

**(3) Percolation.**
$$\mathrm{PERC}_t = \min\big(\mathrm{PERC},\; S_{UZ,t-1} + R_t\big),\qquad
S^{*}_{UZ} = S_{UZ,t-1} + R_t - \mathrm{PERC}_t,\qquad
S^{*}_{LZ} = S_{LZ,t-1} + \mathrm{PERC}_t$$ {#eq-hbv3}

**(4) Response routine** (with the effective constants $K_0^{\text{eff}}=\max(K_0,K_1)$ and
$K_2^{\text{eff}}=\min(K_2,\,0.9K_1)$, see @sec-m3-order):
$$Q_{0,t}=K_0^{\text{eff}}\max\!\big(S^{*}_{UZ}-UZL,\,0\big),\qquad
Q_{1,t}=K_1 S^{*}_{UZ},\qquad
Q_{2,t}=K_2^{\text{eff}} S^{*}_{LZ}$$ {#eq-hbv4}
$$S_{UZ,t} = S^{*}_{UZ}-Q_{0,t}-Q_{1,t},\qquad S_{LZ,t}=S^{*}_{LZ}-Q_{2,t}$$ {#eq-hbv5}
If $Q_{0,t}+Q_{1,t} > S^{*}_{UZ}$ (possible only for extreme $K$ combinations), scale both down by
$S^{*}_{UZ}/(Q_{0,t}+Q_{1,t})$ and set $S_{UZ,t}=0$.

**(5) Routing.** Generated runoff $Q^{\text{gen}}_t = Q_{0,t}+Q_{1,t}+Q_{2,t}$ is convolved with the
triangular weights obtained by integrating the unit-area isosceles triangle $h(u)$ on $[0,\mathrm{MAXBAS}]$:
$$w_j=\int_{j-1}^{j} h(u)\,\mathrm{d}u,\quad j=1..\lceil \mathrm{MAXBAS}\rceil,\qquad
h(u)=\frac{4}{\mathrm{MAXBAS}^2}\min\!\big(u,\ \mathrm{MAXBAS}-u\big)_+ $$ {#eq-hbv6}
$$w_j \leftarrow w_j\Big/\sum_k w_k,\qquad \boxed{\,Q_t=\sum_j w_j\,Q^{\text{gen}}_{t-j+1}\,}$$ {#eq-hbv7}

## Parameter ordering rule {#sec-m3-order}

HBV requires $K_0 \ge K_1 > K_2$. Rectangular bounds are far easier for a global optimizer, so the
**model** enforces the ordering by the monotone maps $K_0^{\text{eff}}=\max(K_0,K_1)$,
$K_2^{\text{eff}}=\min(K_2,0.9K_1)$. The optimizer therefore searches a box; the effective values must be
reported by a13 alongside the raw ones.

## Parameters

```{python}
#| label: tbl-p3
#| tbl-cap: "Slot 3 (HBV-light, no snow) parameters."
ptab(3)
```

## Initial states and warm-up

$SM_0 = 0.60\,FC$; $S_{UZ,0}=5$ mm; $S_{LZ,0}=\min\!\big(400,\;0.40/\max(K_2^{\text{eff}},10^{-4})\big)$ mm
so that the initial baseflow $K_2 S_{LZ}$ is $\approx 0.40$ mm/d — the order of the basin's late-summer low
flow — **derived from the parameter, not from any observation**. UH memory zero.
`warmup_days_min: 365`.

## Mass balance check (builder must test)

$$\sum P - \sum E_a - \sum Q \;=\; \Delta SM + \Delta S_{UZ} + \Delta S_{LZ} + \Delta \mathrm{UH}$$ {#eq-hbv-mb}
with $|\text{residual}| < 10^{-8}$ mm per 1000 days. HBV has no exchange term, so this identity is exact
and is the strongest single test of the implementation.

## Numerical pitfalls

* Compute the recharge with $SM_{t-1}$ (start-of-step storage), then update — swapping the order changes
  the model.
* Cap $SM$ at $FC$ by *transferring* the excess to $R_t$; never discard it.
* $\left(SM/FC\right)^\beta$ with $SM=0$ is 0 for $\beta\ge1$ — fine, but guard $SM\ge0$ anyway.
* Fluxes in @eq-hbv4 are computed from the *pre-update* storages; subtract afterwards (explicit Euler).
* Normalise the MAXBAS weights (@eq-hbv7): the analytic integral of the truncated triangle does not sum to
  1 when $\mathrm{MAXBAS}$ is not an integer.
* `PERC` = 0 is inside the bounds and legal (then $S_{LZ}$ only drains) — do not divide by it.

## Implementation route

From scratch, NumPy daily loop (numba optional; ~50 lines), following @seibert2012 §"Standard version,
soil and response routines". Cross-checks: (i) mass balance @eq-hbv-mb; (ii) with $UZL$ huge and
$K_0=K_1$ the model must collapse to the classic two-linear-reservoir HBV; (iii) with $P=0$ for 200 d the
simulated recession must be a two-exponential mixture with rates $K_1$ and $K_2^{\text{eff}}$ — compare
against the analytic solution.

## Expected behaviour

Strengths: explicit threshold response, two subsurface time scales, strong at-gauge evidence, still cheap
enough for $10^5$ runs. Weaknesses: the lower box is *linear*, so the very-long-tail recession is
exponential rather than power-law; $UZL$/$K_0$ are typically weakly identified in a basin with only 12 %
overland flow, so expect a flat likelihood ridge there (a10: this pair is the main equifinality risk).
**Expected NSE 0.80–0.87 (calibration), 0.74–0.85 (evaluation).**

# Slot 4 — SAC-SMA {#sec-model4}

## Overview

The Sacramento Soil Moisture Accounting model [@burnash1973] is the US National Weather Service River
Forecast System's operational rainfall–runoff model, and the historical test bed of this very data set:
@duan1992 introduced SCE-UA by calibrating SAC-SMA on the Leaf River, @sorooshian1993 studied its data
requirements here, and @boyle2001 its multi-criteria calibration. a01 reports NSE 0.796 for a calibrated
SAC-SMA + Snow-17 at 02472000.

**Why for the Leaf River.** It is the only structure in the portfolio that represents *all* of a01's
process priorities simultaneously: (i) a tension/free-water split in both the upper and the lower zone
(so ET can draw from tension water while free water drains), (ii) a **variable contributing area**
(`ADIMP`) that saturates and generates direct runoff, matching the Dunne 5.1 % / wetland 13.6 %
signature, (iii) a **demand-driven percolation** whose rate rises with lower-zone deficiency
($\mathrm{ZPERC}$, $\mathrm{REXP}$) — a genuine non-linear coupling absent from GR4J and HBV, and
(iv) **two parallel baseflow stores** (`LZFSC`, `LZFPC`) with independent depletion rates, the direct
representation of the 9-d vs 549-d puzzle. Snow-17 is omitted (a01 decision).

## Conceptual diagram

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  P[P] --> IMP["PCTIM·P → ROIMP"]
  P --> ADI[("ADIMC<br/>additional impervious")]
  P --> UZTW[("UZTWC ≤ UZTWM<br/>upper tension")]
  UZTW -->|"excess TWX"| UZFW[("UZFWC ≤ UZFWM<br/>upper free")]
  UZFW -->|"SUR: overflow"| CH
  UZFW -->|"SIF = UZK·UZFWC"| CH
  UZFW -->|"PERC (eq. 4.6)"| SPLIT{"split<br/>PFREE"}
  ADI -->|"ADDRO = PINC·RATIO²"| CH
  SPLIT -->|"1−PFREE"| LZTW[("LZTWC ≤ LZTWM<br/>lower tension")]
  SPLIT -->|"PFREE + LZTW overflow"| LZF{"free-water split<br/>FRACP"}
  LZF --> LZFS[("LZFSC ≤ LZFSM<br/>supplemental")]
  LZF --> LZFP[("LZFPC ≤ LZFPM<br/>primary")]
  LZFS -->|"LZSK·LZFSC"| CH
  LZFP -->|"LZPK·LZFPC"| CH
  IMP --> CH[["total channel inflow TCI"]]
  PET[PET] --> ET["E1 (UZTW) → E2 (UZFW) → E3 (LZTW) → E5 (ADIMC)"]
  ET -.-> UZTW
  ET -.-> UZFW
  ET -.-> LZTW
  ET -.-> ADI
  CH --> UH["gamma UH (UH_N, UH_K)"]
  UH --> Q[["Q (mm/d)"]]
```

## Perceptual → conceptual assumptions

*Represented*: infiltration-excess (via `PCTIM`/upper-zone overflow), saturation-excess on an expanding
area (`ADIMP`), interflow, two baseflow components, tension-water ET demand hierarchy, and
storage-deficiency-driven percolation. *Ignored*: snow, riparian ET (`RIVA` = 0), deep recharge that
bypasses the gauge (`SIDE` = 0), and any spatial distribution.

## Mathematical formulation

**States** (mm): $UZTWC, UZFWC, LZTWC, LZFSC, LZFPC, ADIMC$ and the UH memory.
**Derived constant**: $\mathrm{PAREA} = 1 - \mathrm{PCTIM} - \mathrm{ADIMP}$.
The algorithm below is the NWS `fland1` sequence; it must be implemented exactly in this order.

**(4.1) Evapotranspiration demand hierarchy.** With $E_{\text{dmnd}} = \mathrm{PET}_t$:
$$E_1 = E_{\text{dmnd}}\frac{UZTWC}{UZTWM},\qquad UZTWC \leftarrow UZTWC - E_1,\qquad
\mathrm{RED} = E_{\text{dmnd}}-E_1$$
(if $UZTWC<0$: $E_1 \leftarrow E_1 + UZTWC$, $UZTWC \leftarrow 0$)
$$E_2 = \min(\mathrm{RED},\,UZFWC),\qquad UZFWC \leftarrow UZFWC-E_2,\qquad \mathrm{RED}\leftarrow \mathrm{RED}-E_2$$
**Upper-zone rebalance:** if $UZTWC/UZTWM < UZFWC/UZFWM$, set
$\mathrm{UZRAT}=\dfrac{UZTWC+UZFWC}{UZTWM+UZFWM}$, $UZTWC = UZTWM\cdot \mathrm{UZRAT}$,
$UZFWC = UZFWM\cdot \mathrm{UZRAT}$.
$$E_3 = \mathrm{RED}\,\frac{LZTWC}{UZTWM+LZTWM},\qquad LZTWC \leftarrow LZTWC - E_3 \;(\ge 0)$$ {#eq-sac-et}
**Lower-zone tension resupply:** with $\mathrm{SAVED}=\mathrm{RSERV}(LZFPM+LZFSM)$,
$\mathrm{RATLZT}=LZTWC/LZTWM$ and
$\mathrm{RATLZ}=\dfrac{LZTWC+LZFPC+LZFSC-\mathrm{SAVED}}{LZTWM+LZFPM+LZFSM-\mathrm{SAVED}}$: if
$\mathrm{RATLZT}<\mathrm{RATLZ}$, transfer $\mathrm{DEL}=(\mathrm{RATLZ}-\mathrm{RATLZT})LZTWM$ from
$LZFSC$ (then $LZFPC$ if $LZFSC$ runs out) to $LZTWC$.
**ET from the additional impervious area:**
$$E_5 = E_1 + (\mathrm{RED}+E_2)\frac{ADIMC-E_1-UZTWC}{UZTWM+LZTWM},\qquad ADIMC\leftarrow ADIMC-E_5\;(\ge0),
\qquad E_5 \leftarrow \mathrm{ADIMP}\cdot E_5$$ {#eq-sac-e5}

**(4.2) Precipitation into the upper tension store.**
$$\mathrm{TWX}=\max(P_t + UZTWC - UZTWM,\,0),\qquad
UZTWC = \begin{cases}UZTWC+P_t & \text{if } P_t+UZTWC<UZTWM\\ UZTWM & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}$$
$$ADIMC \leftarrow ADIMC + P_t - \mathrm{TWX},\qquad \mathrm{ROIMP}=P_t\cdot \mathrm{PCTIM}$$ {#eq-sac-twx}

**(4.3) Sub-daily incrementation** (mandatory for stability):
$$N_{\text{inc}} = 1+\left\lfloor 0.2\,(UZFWC+\mathrm{TWX})\right\rfloor,\quad
\Delta = 1/N_{\text{inc}},\quad P_{\text{inc}}=\mathrm{TWX}/N_{\text{inc}}$$
$$D_{UZ}=1-(1-\mathrm{UZK})^{\Delta},\quad D_{LZP}=1-(1-\mathrm{LZPK})^{\Delta},\quad
D_{LZS}=1-(1-\mathrm{LZSK})^{\Delta}$$ {#eq-sac-ninc}

**(4.4) Loop $i=1..N_{\text{inc}}$:**

a. *Additional-impervious direct runoff.*
 $\mathrm{RATIO}=\max\!\big((ADIMC-UZTWC)/LZTWM,\,0\big)$, $\;\mathrm{ADDRO}=P_{\text{inc}}\mathrm{RATIO}^2$.
b. *Baseflow.* $B_p = LZFPC\,D_{LZP}$, $LZFPC \mathrel{-}= B_p$; $B_s = LZFSC\,D_{LZS}$,
 $LZFSC \mathrel{-}= B_s$; accumulate $\mathrm{SBF} \mathrel{+}= B_p+B_s$.
c. *Percolation* (only if $P_{\text{inc}}+UZFWC>2\cdot10^{-6}$):
$$\mathrm{PERCM}=LZFPM\,D_{LZP}+LZFSM\,D_{LZS},\qquad
\mathrm{DEFR}=1-\frac{LZTWC+LZFPC+LZFSC}{LZTWM+LZFPM+LZFSM}$$
$$\mathrm{PERC}=\mathrm{PERCM}\Big(1+\mathrm{ZPERC}\,\mathrm{DEFR}^{\mathrm{REXP}}\Big)\frac{UZFWC}{UZFWM}$$ {#eq-sac-perc}
 capped by $\mathrm{PERC}\le UZFWC$ and by the remaining remaining lower-zone capacity; then
 $UZFWC \mathrel{-}= \mathrm{PERC}$.
d. *Interflow.* $\;\mathrm{DEL}=UZFWC\,D_{UZ}$, $\;\mathrm{SIF}\mathrel{+}=\mathrm{DEL}$,
 $\;UZFWC\mathrel{-}=\mathrm{DEL}$.
e. *Distribute percolation.* $\mathrm{PERCT}=\mathrm{PERC}(1-\mathrm{PFREE})$ goes to $LZTWC$ (overflow
 $\mathrm{PERCF}$ carries on); $\mathrm{PERCF}\mathrel{+}=\mathrm{PERC}\cdot\mathrm{PFREE}$. Split
 $\mathrm{PERCF}$ between the two free-water stores with
$$\mathrm{HPL}=\frac{LZFPM}{LZFPM+LZFSM},\quad
\mathrm{FRACP}=\min\!\left(1,\ \mathrm{HPL}\,\frac{2(1-LZFPC/LZFPM)}{(1-LZFPC/LZFPM)+(1-LZFSC/LZFSM)}\right)$$ {#eq-sac-fracp}
 $\mathrm{PERCP}=\mathrm{FRACP}\cdot\mathrm{PERCF}$ → $LZFPC$, remainder → $LZFSC$; any overflow of either
 store is returned to $LZTWC$.
f. *Surface runoff.* If $P_{\text{inc}}+UZFWC>UZFWM$:
 $\mathrm{SUR}=P_{\text{inc}}+UZFWC-UZFWM$, $UZFWC=UZFWM$,
 $\mathrm{SSUR}\mathrel{+}=\mathrm{SUR}\cdot \mathrm{PAREA}$,
 $\mathrm{ADSUR}=\mathrm{SUR}\left(1-\mathrm{ADDRO}/P_{\text{inc}}\right)$,
 $\mathrm{SSUR}\mathrel{+}=\mathrm{ADSUR}\cdot\mathrm{ADIMP}$; else $UZFWC\mathrel{+}=P_{\text{inc}}$,
 $\mathrm{ADSUR}=0$.
g. *ADIMC update.* $ADIMC \mathrel{+}= P_{\text{inc}}-\mathrm{ADDRO}-\mathrm{ADSUR}$; if
 $ADIMC>UZTWM+LZTWM$, move the excess to $\mathrm{ADDRO}$ and cap. Accumulate
 $\mathrm{SDRO}\mathrel{+}=\mathrm{ADDRO}\cdot\mathrm{ADIMP}$.

**(4.5) Channel inflow.**
$$\mathrm{TCI}_t = \mathrm{ROIMP} + \mathrm{SDRO} + \mathrm{SSUR} + \mathrm{SIF}\cdot \mathrm{PAREA}
+ \frac{\mathrm{SBF}\cdot \mathrm{PAREA}}{1+\mathrm{SIDE}}$$ {#eq-sac-tci}
with $\mathrm{SIDE}=0$ here. Total ET: $\mathrm{TET}_t=(E_1+E_2+E_3)\mathrm{PAREA}+E_5$
(plus $E_4=0$ since $\mathrm{RIVA}=0$).

**(4.6) Routing — 2-parameter gamma (Nash) unit hydrograph** [@nash1957]:
$$u_j = F_\Gamma\!\big(j;\,\mathrm{UH\_N},\mathrm{UH\_K}\big)-F_\Gamma\!\big(j-1;\,\mathrm{UH\_N},\mathrm{UH\_K}\big),
\qquad j = 1..n_{uh},\qquad u_j \leftarrow u_j\Big/\textstyle\sum_k u_k$$ {#eq-sac-uh}
$$\boxed{\,Q_t=\sum_{j=1}^{n_{uh}} u_j\,\mathrm{TCI}_{t-j+1}\,},\qquad
n_{uh}=\min\!\big(60,\ \min\{n: F_\Gamma(n)\ge0.9999\}\big)$$
Mean lag $=\mathrm{UH\_N}\cdot\mathrm{UH\_K}$ days, which the bounds place at 0.1–15 d with a prior of
1–3 d (a01).

## Parameters

```{python}

#| tbl-cap: "Slot 4 (SAC-SMA) free parameters. Ranges follow the DREAM manual Ex. 23 set quoted by a01, widened for PFREE (0–0.6) and PCTIM narrowed to 0–0.05 given the 0.41 % measured impervious cover."
ptab(4)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-p4fix
#| tbl-cap: "Slot 4 fixed (non-calibrated) parameters."
m4 = [x for x in MODELS["models"] if x["slot"] == 4][0]
pd.DataFrame([{"name": k, "value": v["value"], "why": v["description"]} for k, v in m4["fixed_parameters"].items()])
```

## Initial states and warm-up

$UZTWC=0.5\,UZTWM$, $UZFWC=0.1\,UZFWM$, $LZTWC=0.6\,LZTWM$, $LZFSC=0.2\,LZFSM$, $LZFPC=0.6\,LZFPM$,
$ADIMC=UZTWC+LZTWC$ (a required consistency condition), UH memory zero. All parameter-derived.
`warmup_days_min: 730` — with $\mathrm{LZPK}\approx0.004$ d⁻¹ the primary store has $\tau\approx250$ d, so
one year is not enough to forget the initial condition inside the calibration window. (In the
**evaluation** window only 92 d are available for *every* model; that is a property of the experiment, not
of this slot, and a16 must interpret it as such.)

## Mass balance check (builder must test)

$$\sum P - \sum \mathrm{TET} - \sum \mathrm{TCI} \;=\;
\mathrm{PAREA}\,\Delta\!\left(UZTWC+UZFWC+LZTWC+LZFSC+LZFPC\right) + \mathrm{ADIMP}\,\Delta ADIMC
+ \Delta \mathrm{UH}$$ {#eq-sac-mb}
Tolerance $10^{-6}$ mm per 1000 days. Test it with $\mathrm{PCTIM}=\mathrm{ADIMP}=0$ first (then
$\mathrm{PAREA}=1$ and the identity simplifies), then with $\mathrm{ADIMP}=0.3$.

## Numerical pitfalls

* **Never skip the sub-daily incrementation** (@eq-sac-ninc). With a 100 mm/d storm (the record maximum is
  221.5 mm/d, a02) a single explicit step drains the upper zone by more than its content.
* Convert depletion rates with $1-(1-K)^{\Delta}$, **not** $K\Delta$.
* Guard every store: `if abs(x) < 1e-10: x = 0`, and return the clipped amount to the flux that caused it.
* Assert $UZTWC \le ADIMC \le UZTWM+LZTWM$ every step; violating it is the classic SAC-SMA coding bug.
* In step (f) $\mathrm{ADDRO}/P_{\text{inc}}$ divides by zero when $P_{\text{inc}}=0$; that branch is only
  reached when $P_{\text{inc}}>0$, but code the guard explicitly.
* $\mathrm{DEFR}$ can be slightly negative from round-off → `max(DEFR, 0)` before the power in @eq-sac-perc
  ($\mathrm{REXP}$ may be fractional).
* @eq-sac-fracp divides by $(1-LZFPC/LZFPM)+(1-LZFSC/LZFSM)$, which is 0 when both stores are full;
  guard with $\max(\cdot,10^{-9})$ and clamp $\mathrm{FRACP}\in[0,1]$.
* `numba.njit` the daily loop; a pure-Python loop is ~100× too slow for $10^4$–$10^5$ optimizer runs
  (@sec-compute).

## Implementation route

From scratch, NumPy + `numba.njit`, following @burnash1973 and the NWS `fland1` ordering reproduced above;
~200 lines. Use `scipy.stats.gamma.cdf` once per parameter set for @eq-sac-uh. `config/project.yaml`
carries `external_references.sacsma_numba_path` (currently `null`); if the user later supplies an existing
Numba SAC-SMA, a08 should use it **only as a test oracle**, not as the deliverable. Validation:
(i) @eq-sac-mb; (ii) with $\mathrm{ADIMP}=\mathrm{PCTIM}=0$ and a 200-day dry spell the recession must be
the sum of two exponentials with rates $\mathrm{LZSK}$ and $\mathrm{LZPK}$; (iii) simulated BFI
(Lyne–Hollick, $\alpha = 0.925$, 3 passes) with default parameters should land in 0.3–0.6.

## Expected behaviour

Strengths: the most complete process representation available on P/PET alone; two baseflow time scales;
the only structure able to separate "soil is wet but not saturated" from "saturated area is expanding".
Weaknesses: 15 parameters with well-documented equifinality (a01: `LZPK`-type parameters are the classic
ill-identified ones here; @sorooshian1993), a rough response surface (thresholds and the
$N_{\text{inc}}$ switch make it **non-smooth** → derivative-free global search only, see @sec-a10), and
~4× the run time of GR4J. **Expected NSE 0.82–0.88 (calibration), 0.74–0.85 (evaluation).**

# Slot 5 — single-basin sequence-to-sequence LSTM {#sec-model5}

## Overview

A Long Short-Term Memory network [@hochreiter1997] applied to rainfall–runoff modelling following
@kratzert2018 and @kratzert2019. The LSTM's cell state acts as a learned, multi-dimensional storage system
whose "recharge" and "release" are gated by the forcing — conceptually the same role as the stores in slots
2–4, but with the partitioning learned rather than prescribed. @kratzert2019 report NSE 0.84–0.86 for a
*regional* LSTM at this exact gauge; here we have only one basin, so the design is heavily regularised.

**Why for the Leaf River.** (i) It is the only family in the portfolio whose errors are not generated by a
prescribed store-and-release structure, which is what makes the ensembles in @sec-ensembles worth testing.
(ii) a02's memory analysis (linear $R^2$ still rising at a 365-day lag) says the basin has exactly the kind
of long, non-linear memory an LSTM is built for. (iii) 36 calibration water years is at the lower edge of
single-basin feasibility, which is why dropout, weight decay, early stopping and 5-seed averaging are all
prescribed rather than optional.

## Conceptual diagram

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph IN["inputs at day t (standardised, calibration stats)"]
    A["P_std, PET_std"]
    B["sin/cos(2π·doy/365.25)"]
    C["optional: API(0.98,0.93,0.80),<br/>ΣP(7,30,90,365),<br/>Σ(P−PET)(30,90,365)"]
  end
  IN --> L["LSTM cell<br/>h_t, c_t  (H = 32..128)"]
  L -->|"h_t-1, c_t-1"| L
  L --> D["dropout"]
  D --> H["Linear(H → 1) → ŷ_t"]
  H --> S["Q̂_t = softplus(μ_Q + σ_Q·ŷ_t)"]
  S --> O[["Q̂_t (mm/d) > 0"]]
```

## Perceptual → conceptual assumptions

*Represented*: multi-scale memory of rainfall and evaporative demand, a learned non-linear
wetness-dependent response, and seasonality (through PET and the harmonics).
*Ignored/absent*: mass conservation, interpretable stores, any guarantee of behaviour outside the
calibration input distribution. The evaluation window is 1.29× wetter in the mean than calibration but
does **not** exceed the calibration flow magnitudes (a02), so the extrapolation risk is bounded but real.

## Mathematical formulation

**Inputs.** Base features (always):
$$\mathbf{x}_t = \Big[\tfrac{P_t-3.9078}{10.1414},\;\tfrac{\mathrm{PET}_t-2.9004}{1.8890},\;
\sin\tfrac{2\pi d_t}{365.25},\;\cos\tfrac{2\pi d_t}{365.25}\Big]$$ {#eq-lstm-x}
If `use_antecedent_features` = 1, ten more columns are appended: $A^{(\lambda)}_t=\lambda A^{(\lambda)}_{t-1}+P_t$
for $\lambda\in\{0.98,0.93,0.80\}$; $\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}P_{t-i}$ for $k\in\{7,30,90,365\}$; and
$\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(P_{t-i}-\mathrm{PET}_{t-i})$ for $k\in\{30,90,365\}$. **Each of these ten is standardised
with its own mean/sd computed on the calibration metric window only** and frozen in the model artefact.

**Cell.** Standard LSTM equations, with $\sigma$ the logistic function and $\odot$ the Hadamard product:
$$\mathbf{i}_t=\sigma(W_i\mathbf{x}_t+U_i\mathbf{h}_{t-1}+\mathbf{b}_i),\qquad
\mathbf{f}_t=\sigma(W_f\mathbf{x}_t+U_f\mathbf{h}_{t-1}+\mathbf{b}_f)$$ {#eq-lstm-if}
$$\mathbf{g}_t=\tanh(W_g\mathbf{x}_t+U_g\mathbf{h}_{t-1}+\mathbf{b}_g),\qquad
\mathbf{o}_t=\sigma(W_o\mathbf{x}_t+U_o\mathbf{h}_{t-1}+\mathbf{b}_o)$$ {#eq-lstm-go}
$$\mathbf{c}_t=\mathbf{f}_t\odot\mathbf{c}_{t-1}+\mathbf{i}_t\odot\mathbf{g}_t,\qquad
\mathbf{h}_t=\mathbf{o}_t\odot\tanh(\mathbf{c}_t)$$ {#eq-lstm-c}

**Head and output transform** ($\mu_Q=1.3533$, $\sigma_Q=2.8511$ mm/d from the calibration window):
$$\hat y_t=\mathbf{w}^\top \mathrm{Dropout}(\mathbf{h}_t)+b,\qquad
\boxed{\;\hat Q_t=\mathrm{softplus}\!\big(\mu_Q+\sigma_Q\,\hat y_t\big)=\ln\!\big(1+e^{\mu_Q+\sigma_Q\hat y_t}\big)\;}$$ {#eq-lstm-out}
The softplus guarantees $\hat Q_t>0$ (the river is perennial, a02) *and* keeps the gradient alive for the
log-space loss term, which a hard clip would not.

**Loss** ($\sigma_{\log Q}=1.2192$):
$$\mathcal{L}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{T}|}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\left(\frac{\hat Q_t-Q_t}{\sigma_Q}\right)^{2}
\;+\;w_{\log}\,\frac{1}{|\mathcal{T}|}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}
\left(\frac{\ln(\hat Q_t+10^{-6})-\ln Q_t}{\sigma_{\log Q}}\right)^{2}$$ {#eq-lstm-loss}
The first term is the NSE-equivalent objective on the reported metric; the second (weight $w_{\log}$,
default 0.25) protects the 40 % of days below 0.45 mm/d that the first term ignores (a02: the wettest 5 %
of days carry 40 % of the volume). $\mathcal{T}$ excludes the first `warmup_steps` of every training window.

**Sequence handling.** Training draws random contiguous windows of length `seq_len` (default 365 d)
from the *internal-train* mask; the loss is evaluated only on steps
$t>$ `warmup_steps` (default 60), so the network learns to be accurate given as little as 60 days of
context. At **inference** the model performs a *single continuous forward pass* over whatever frame
`simulate()` receives, with $\mathbf{h}_0=\mathbf{c}_0=\mathbf{0}$, emitting one $\hat Q_t$ per day. This
is what makes the LSTM comparable to the conceptual slots in the evaluation window, where only 92 warm-up
days exist before the metric period begins (a01/a16 note).

## Hyperparameters

```{python}
#| label: tbl-p5
#| tbl-cap: "Slot 5 hyperparameters exposed to a15. The ~20,000 network weights are fitted by Adam, not searched."
ptab(5)
```

Fixed (not searched): `max_epochs` 200, early-stopping patience 20, gradient-norm clip 1.0, lr $\times$ 0.5
at epochs 60 and 120, seeds 42–46 (5 ensemble members, output = arithmetic mean of the members' $\hat Q$).

## Initial states and warm-up

$\mathbf{h}_0=\mathbf{c}_0=\mathbf{0}$ (no observation enters). `warmup_days_min: 90`; the warm-up
masking during training is what makes this defensible.

## Mass balance check

Not applicable. Required assertions instead: $\hat Q_t>0\ \forall t$ and
$0.85\le\overline{\hat Q}/\overline{Q}\le1.15$ on the calibration metric window. a09 must **additionally**
test that a continuous forward pass and a chunked pass with 365 d of context agree to $<10^{-3}$ mm/d after
the first 90 days — if they do not, the model has learned a state drift and `seq_len` must be raised.

## Numerical pitfalls

* **Leakage**: training windows must be drawn from `internal_mask(frame, "train")` only, and the
  standardisation constants must come from `config/models.yaml → scaling:` — never recomputed on the frame
  given at prediction time. `load()` must restore them; a silent re-standardisation on the evaluation
  frame would invalidate the whole study.
* Use `torch.nn.functional.softplus` (numerically stable for large arguments), and
  $\ln(\hat Q+10^{-6})$ in @eq-lstm-loss.
* MPS is not bit-reproducible for all kernels; set `torch.manual_seed(seed)` per member, and if the
  5-member mean is not reproducible across runs, fall back to `cpu` and record it in the a09/a15 handoff
  (CLAUDE.md rule 7). Device via `src.common.data.torch_device()`.
* Round `hidden_size`, `n_layers`, `seq_len`, `warmup_steps`, `batch_size`,
  `use_antecedent_features` to integers when they arrive from a continuous optimizer.
* The rolling 365-day features need 365 leading days; inside the *evaluation* frame those do not exist —
  compute them with a growing (partial) window and divide by the number of available days, i.e.
  `pandas.Series.rolling(k, min_periods=1).mean() * k`. Document the choice; it is applied identically in
  calibration and evaluation.

## Implementation route

`torch` 2.13.0 (BSD-3). `kind: "trainable"`: `fit(forcing, target, params)` trains the 5 members;
`simulate(forcing, params)` runs the continuous pass and averages them; `save`/`load` persist
`state_dict`s + scaling constants + hyperparameters. Same lazy-fit rule as slot 1 (fit on the calibration
window through `src.common.data` if unfitted; never on evaluation data).
Compute budget: with 10,592 training days, `seq_len` 365 and batch 256 there are ~41 minibatches per epoch;
at ≤200 epochs and 5 seeds this is well inside the 3 h limit (@sec-compute).

## Expected behaviour

Strengths: the highest ceiling in the portfolio and a genuinely different error structure. Weaknesses:
~1.9 fitted weights per training day → overfitting is the main risk; no mass conservation, so the
water-balance ($\beta$) term of KGE is not protected structurally; and behaviour in the wetter evaluation
period is an empirical question. **Expected NSE 0.85–0.92 (calibration), 0.75–0.87 (evaluation)** — note
the deliberately wide evaluation band: this is the slot with the largest calibration-to-evaluation drop
risk.

Two readings of the matrix matter for a16:

* **No process required by @tbl-constraints is missing from the portfolio**, and each of the five hard
  requirements is covered by at least two slots — so a failure of one slot cannot be blamed on a missing
  process at the portfolio level.
* The **complementarity** is concentrated where it should be: only SAC-SMA has the tension/free split and
  an explicit second baseflow store; only GR4J has the exchange term; only HBV has a pure threshold
  outlet; only the LSTM has a learned response; only slot 1 has no state at all.

## Response-function shapes

```{python}
#| label: fig-shapes
#| fig-cap: "Left: runoff-generation functions — the fraction of incoming rain that becomes runoff as a function of relative soil storage (GR4J eq. 2.2 with x1 = 350 mm and Pn = 10 mm/d; HBV eq. 3.1 for beta = 1, 2, 4). Right: routing kernels at their default parameters (GR4J UH1/UH2 with x4 = 1.7 d, HBV triangle with MAXBAS = 2.5 d, SAC-SMA gamma UH with N = 2, K = 0.6 d). All kernels sum to 1."
from scipy.stats import gamma as gammadist
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.1))
s = np.linspace(0, 1, 200)
x1, Pn = 350.0, 10.0
th = np.tanh(Pn / x1)
Ps = x1 * (1 - s**2) * th / (1 + s * th)
axes[0].plot(s, 1 - Ps / Pn, lw=2.2, label="GR4J: 1 - Ps/Pn  (x1=350, Pn=10)")
for b in [1, 2, 4]:
    axes[0].plot(s, s**b, lw=1.8, ls="--", label=f"HBV: (SM/FC)^beta, beta={b}")
axes[0].set_xlabel("relative soil storage  S/x1  or  SM/FC")
axes[0].set_ylabel("fraction of rain becoming recharge/runoff")
axes[0].set_title("Runoff-generation functions"); axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)

j = np.arange(1, 13)
x4 = 1.7
SH1 = lambda u: np.clip((u / x4) ** 2.5, 0, 1) * (u < x4) + 1.0 * (u >= x4)
def SH2(u):
    u = np.asarray(u, float); out = np.where(u < x4, 0.5 * np.clip(u / x4, 0, None) ** 2.5,
        np.where(u < 2 * x4, 1 - 0.5 * np.clip(2 - u / x4, 0, None) ** 2.5, 1.0))
    return np.clip(out, 0, 1)
u1 = np.diff(np.concatenate([[0.], SH1(j)])); u2 = np.diff(np.concatenate([[0.], SH2(j)]))
mb = 2.5
h = lambda u: (4 / mb**2) * np.clip(np.minimum(u, mb - u), 0, None)
from scipy.integrate import quad
wt = np.array([quad(h, k - 1, k)[0] for k in j]); wt /= wt.sum()
ug = np.diff(np.concatenate([[0.], gammadist.cdf(j, 2.0, scale=0.6)])); ug /= ug.sum()
w = 0.2
axes[1].bar(j - 1.5 * w, u1, w, label="GR4J UH1 (x4=1.7)")
axes[1].bar(j - 0.5 * w, u2, w, label="GR4J UH2 (2x4)")
axes[1].bar(j + 0.5 * w, wt, w, label="HBV triangle (MAXBAS=2.5)")
axes[1].bar(j + 1.5 * w, ug, w, label="SAC-SMA gamma (N=2, K=0.6)")
axes[1].set_xlim(0.3, 8.7); axes[1].set_xlabel("lag (days)"); axes[1].set_ylabel("ordinate")
axes[1].set_title("Routing kernels (defaults)"); axes[1].legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(FIG / "a03_response_shapes.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.show()
print("kernel sums:", [round(float(v.sum()), 12) for v in (u1, u2, wt, ug)])
print("mean lags (d):", {"GR4J UH1": float((j*u1).sum()), "GR4J UH2": float((j*u2).sum()),
                         "HBV": float((j*wt).sum()), "SAC-SMA": float((j*ug).sum())})
```

All four default kernels place their mass at 1–3 days, consistent with the observed onset lag of 1 d and
$P\!\to\!Q$ cross-correlation peak at 3 d (a02).

# Compute budget: a timing prototype {#sec-compute}

a10 must size the global search against a hard 3 h wall-time limit per optimizer. The following is a
**non-authoritative** reference implementation of GR4J written only to measure cost — a06 writes the
deliverable version in `src/models/model_2.py`. It runs on the **calibration** window only.

```{python}
#| label: timing
#| code-fold: show
df   = load_data()
cal  = slice_run(df, "calibration")           # 1951-10-01..1988-09-30
mask = metric_mask(cal, "calibration")        # 1952-10-01..1988-09-30
P, E, Qobs = cal["P"].to_numpy(), cal["PET"].to_numpy(), cal["Q"].to_numpy()
print(f"calibration run window: {cal.index[0].date()}..{cal.index[-1].date()}  n={len(cal)}  metric days={mask.sum()}")

def gr4j_uh(x4):
    nu1, nu2 = int(np.ceil(x4)), int(np.ceil(2 * x4))
    jj1, jj2 = np.arange(nu1 + 1.0), np.arange(nu2 + 1.0)
    sh1 = np.where(jj1 < x4, np.clip(jj1 / x4, 0, None) ** 2.5, 1.0)
    sh2 = np.where(jj2 < x4, 0.5 * np.clip(jj2 / x4, 0, None) ** 2.5,
          np.where(jj2 < 2 * x4, 1 - 0.5 * np.clip(2 - jj2 / x4, 0, None) ** 2.5, 1.0))
    u1, u2 = np.diff(sh1), np.diff(sh2)
    return u1 / u1.sum(), u2 / u2.sum()

def gr4j_core(P, E, x1, x2, x3, u1, u2):
    """Non-authoritative timing prototype (a06 writes the deliverable). Perrin et al. (2003)."""
    n = P.shape[0]
    nu1, nu2 = u1.shape[0], u2.shape[0]
    S, R = 0.30 * x1, 0.50 * x3
    m1 = np.zeros(nu1); m2 = np.zeros(nu2)
    Q = np.empty(n)
    for t in range(n):
        p = P[t]; e = E[t]
        if p >= e:
            pn = p - e; en = 0.0
        else:
            pn = 0.0; en = e - p
        s = S / x1
        ps = 0.0; es = 0.0
        if pn > 0.0:
            th = np.tanh(min(pn / x1, 13.0))
            ps = x1 * (1.0 - s * s) * th / (1.0 + s * th)
        else:
            th = np.tanh(min(en / x1, 13.0))
            es = S * (2.0 - s) * th / (1.0 + (1.0 - s) * th)
        S = S - es + ps
        perc = S * (1.0 - (1.0 + (4.0 / 9.0 * S / x1) ** 4) ** -0.25)
        S -= perc
        pr = perc + (pn - ps)
        q9 = m1[0] + 0.9 * pr * u1[0]
        for k in range(nu1 - 1):
            m1[k] = m1[k + 1] + 0.9 * pr * u1[k + 1]
        m1[nu1 - 1] = 0.0
        q1 = m2[0] + 0.1 * pr * u2[0]
        for k in range(nu2 - 1):
            m2[k] = m2[k + 1] + 0.1 * pr * u2[k + 1]
        m2[nu2 - 1] = 0.0
        f = x2 * (R / x3) ** 3.5
        R = R + q9 + f
        if R < 0.0:
            R = 0.0
        qr = R * (1.0 - (1.0 + (R / x3) ** 4) ** -0.25)
        R -= qr
        qd = q1 + f
        if qd < 0.0:
            qd = 0.0
        Q[t] = qr + qd
    return Q

u1, u2 = gr4j_uh(1.7)
t0 = time.perf_counter(); Qs = gr4j_core(P, E, 350., 0., 90., u1, u2); t_np = time.perf_counter() - t0
res = {"numpy/python loop [s/run]": t_np}
try:
    from numba import njit
    gr4j_nb = njit(cache=False)(gr4j_core)
    _ = gr4j_nb(P[:50], E[:50], 350., 0., 90., u1, u2)          # compile
    t0 = time.perf_counter(); Qn = gr4j_nb(P, E, 350., 0., 90., u1, u2)
    res["numba [s/run]"] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    res["speed-up"] = t_np / res["numba [s/run]"]
    res["python-vs-numba max |diff| [mm/d]"] = float(np.max(np.abs(Qn - Qs)))
except Exception as ex:
    res["numba"] = f"unavailable: {type(ex).__name__}: {ex}"
res["UH ordinate sums (must be 1)"] = f"{u1.sum():.12f} / {u2.sum():.12f}"
res["NSE, DEFAULT (uncalibrated) parameters, calibration metric window"] = float(nse(Qs[mask], Qobs[mask]))
res["KGE, DEFAULT parameters"] = float(kge_components(Qs[mask], Qobs[mask])["KGE"])
res["mean sim / mean obs"] = float(Qs[mask].mean() / Qobs[mask].mean())
pd.Series(res).to_frame("value")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-budget
#| fig-cap: "Wall-clock budget for a global search. Bars show the estimated time for 10,000 / 50,000 / 100,000 model evaluations given the measured GR4J cost and the per-model cost factors assumed in the text; the dashed line is the 3 h limit of config/project.yaml."
per_run = res.get("numba [s/run]", res["numpy/python loop [s/run]"])
factors = {"2 GR4J": 1.0, "3 HBV": 1.2, "4 SAC-SMA": 4.0, "1 ARX-API (ridge solve)": 0.8}
runs = [10_000, 50_000, 100_000]
B = pd.DataFrame({f"{r//1000}k runs": {k: per_run * f * r / 3600 for k, f in factors.items()} for r in runs})
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.6))
B.plot(kind="bar", ax=ax); ax.axhline(3, ls="--", c="crimson"); ax.text(3.1, 3.05, "3 h limit", color="crimson", fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel("wall time [h], single core"); ax.set_title("Estimated global-search cost (single core; LR_N_JOBS cores divide it)")
plt.xticks(rotation=12); plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(FIG / "a03_compute_budget.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.show()
B.round(3)
```

Cost factors are estimates: HBV has fewer operations per step than GR4J but an extra convolution
(≈1.2×); SAC-SMA runs $N_{\text{inc}}$ sub-steps per day (typically 1–10 on wet days, ≈4× on average);
slot 1 costs one feature build plus a $22\times22$ Cholesky solve. Slot 5 is not in the bar chart because
it is trained, not searched: ~41 minibatches/epoch × ≤200 epochs × 5 seeds.

# Pre-declared ensembles for a16 {#sec-ensembles}

These are declared **now**, before any calibration result exists, so that no evaluation or hindsight
information can influence them (CLAUDE.md rule 3 and `config/project.yaml → ensembles_and_hybrids_allowed`).
They are stored verbatim in `config/models.yaml → ensembles:`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ens
#| tbl-cap: "Pre-declared ensembles. All weights are either fixed a priori or fitted on calibration data only."
pd.DataFrame([{"id": e["id"], "members (slots)": str(e["members"]),
               "weights": str(e["weights"]), "rationale": e["description"]} for e in MODELS["ensembles"]])
```

`ens_nnls_calibration` is the only one with fitted weights: non-negative least squares of the five
simulated series against observed $Q$ on the **internal validation** window 1981-10-01…1988-09-30
(2,557 days, never used to fit any member's parameters), rescaled to sum to 1. This follows the classical
multi-model combination results of @shamseldin1997 and mirrors the hybrid-model gains reported by
@konapala2020, without incurring the implementation risk of a differentiable hybrid (@sec-why).

# Build-phase evidence that puts H1 at risk {#sec-h1-risk}

::: {.callout-important}
## Added after P4 by the orchestrator, on the user's instruction

This section was **not** written by a03 during model design. It was added once all five slots had been
built (phase P4) because the build-phase numbers already bear on hypothesis **H1** in
@sec-hypotheses, and pre-registration is worthless if inconvenient evidence is quietly folded in later.
The finding was raised by a05 as **ISSUE-004** in `context/ISSUES.md`.
:::

## The finding

H1 predicts `NSE(slot 1) < NSE(slot 2)`: the 19-coefficient ARX–API ridge regression was included as the
*floor* of the complexity gradient, with an expected calibration band of NSE 0.60–0.75
(@tbl-summary). It does not behave like a floor.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-h1-risk
#| tbl-cap: "Build-phase performance of the five slots at their DEFAULT (uncalibrated) settings, calibration metric window 1952-10-01..1988-09-30 (13,149 d). Read live from the builders' handoff JSONs. Slot 5 is a 30-of-200-epoch smoke run, so it is a lower bound; slots 2-4 are pure defaults and will improve substantially under calibration."
import json, pandas as pd
rows = []
for agent, slot, name, band in [("a05", 1, "ARX-API ridge", "0.60-0.75"),
                                ("a06", 2, "GR4J",          "0.78-0.86"),
                                ("a07", 3, "HBV-light",     "0.80-0.87"),
                                ("a08", 4, "SAC-SMA",       "0.82-0.88"),
                                ("a09", 5, "LSTM",          "0.85-0.92")]:
    k = json.load(open(ROOT / "context" / "handoffs" / f"{agent}.json")).get("key_numbers", {})
    rows.append({"slot": slot, "model": name,
                 "objective": k.get("smoke_objective_cal_default"),
                 "KGE": k.get("smoke_KGE_cal_default"),
                 "NSE": k.get("smoke_NSE_cal_default"),
                 "a03 expected NSE_cal": band})
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("slot")
```

At its *default* hyperparameters slot 1 reaches **NSE 0.8425 / KGE 0.8849** on the calibration metric
window — above the top of its predicted band and above every conceptual slot at *their* defaults. The
comparison that matters more is out-of-sample: fitted on internal train (1952-10-01…1981-09-30) and scored
on internal validation (1981-10-01…1988-09-30), slot 1 gives **KGE 0.8718 / NSE 0.8590**
(objective 0.8654). For scale, a01's independent benchmarks *at this same gauge* are calibrated SAC-SMA
NSE 0.796, calibrated HBV 0.819, and a regional LSTM 0.84–0.86.

So a linear model in transformed space, with no soil-moisture store and no mass balance, is currently
sitting inside the band that published deep-learning models occupy on this basin.

## Why this is not leakage

An out-of-band result of this kind is usually a leak, so it was checked structurally rather than argued
away. Four things were verified in `src/models/model_1.py`:

1. **Observed discharge never enters the design matrix.** The regressors are precipitation, PET and
   exponentially-weighted antecedent-precipitation indices. The "AR" in ARX is autoregression in the API
   *state*, not on observed $Q$ — so the model remains comparable with the conceptual slots, which is
   exactly what `config/project.yaml -> ml_state_note` requires.
2. **The multiplicative bias factor $c$ is frozen at fit time.** It is computed once inside `fit()` from
   the fitting window and only *read* in `simulate()`. It is not recomputed from the window being
   predicted — which would have been a textbook leak, and would have manufactured $\beta \approx 1$ on any
   period.
3. **Column means and standard deviations are likewise frozen** in `_fitted` and restored by `load()`.
4. **The lazy-fit fallback routes to the calibration window** through the guarded loader, never to the
   window passed to `simulate()`. The leak-safe path is the default, not an option.

The evaluation window played no part in any of this: `src/common/data.py` raises `PermissionError` unless
`LR_AGENT=a16`, and no test or model sets that variable.

## What it does and does not imply

It does **not** yet falsify H1. Two reasons to withhold judgement until a16:

- These are calibration-period and *internal-validation* numbers. H1 is stated on the evaluation metric
  window 1949-01-01…1951-09-30, which no agent except a16 may touch.
- That window is the **wettest stretch of the record** — mean $Q$ ratio 1.29 versus calibration, runoff
  ratio 0.41 against 0.35 (a02). A regression carries no mass balance and no storage ceiling, so it has
  more room to degrade under a wetness shift than a conceptual model does. The conceptual slots also
  arrive at a16 *calibrated*, whereas the numbers above are mostly defaults.

What it does imply is that the interesting question has moved. The study was designed to measure how much
complexity buys; it may instead measure **how little**. If slot 1 holds its ground on the evaluation
window, the honest headline is that on a humid, energy-limited, snow-free basin with 40 years of clean
forcing, a well-posed linear model in transformed space is competitive with conceptual hydrology — and
H1, as pre-registered, is falsified in its first clause.

a16 must report that outcome plainly if it occurs, including the possibility that
`NSE(slot 1) > NSE(slot 4)`. A pre-registered hypothesis that fails is a result, not an error.

# Instructions to downstream agents {#sec-a10}

## Builders a05–a09

* Subclass `src.common.model_api.BaseModel`; set `model_id` to the slot `id` and `kind` exactly as in
  `config/models.yaml`. `simulate()` returns a `pd.Series` of mm/day **on the full input index**
  (warm-up included), deterministic given parameters and seed.
* **Read parameter bounds/defaults from `config/models.yaml`, do not hard-code them**; expose them through
  `param_specs()` as `ParamSpec` objects (`log_scale=True` where the YAML says so).
* Load data only via `src.common.data`; never call `slice_run(..., "evaluation")`.
* Ship the mass-balance test of your section as a `pytest` case in `tests/test_model_N.py`, plus
  (i) a determinism test (two identical calls give bitwise-identical output), (ii) a bounds test
  (`defaults()` inside `bounds()`), (iii) a 200-day dry-spell recession test against the analytic solution
  where one exists.
* Integer-valued parameters (`integer: true` in the YAML) must be rounded inside the model, so the
  optimizer can keep searching a continuous box.

## Optimizer advisor a10

```{python}

 (1, "arx_api_ridge", 7, "smooth in lam_*/bc_lambda, PIECEWISE-CONSTANT in n_lag (integer)",

 (3, "hbv_light", 9, "NON-SMOOTH: the UZL threshold and the K-ordering maps max()/min() create kinks",
  "Derivative-free global search only (SCE-UA, DE, DDS). Expect a flat ridge in (UZL, K0) - report the marginal sensitivity, not just the optimum."),
 (4, "sacsma", 15, "NON-SMOOTH and high-dimensional: thresholds, store caps, and the integer N_inc switch",
  "This is the original SCE-UA benchmark problem (Duan et al. 1992) - use SCE-UA with >= 2*15+1 complexes or DE with a large population; budget 5e4-1e5 evaluations. Numba is mandatory to stay inside 3 h."),
 (5, "lstm_seq2seq", 10, "network weights: SMOOTH, gradient-based (Adam). Hyperparameters: mixed integer, expensive (~10-20 min per full training)",
  "Two-level problem: Adam for the weights (do NOT hand the weights to a global optimizer), and <= 25 hyperparameter trials with Optuna TPE / random search on the internal-validation loss. Early stopping counts as part of the fit."),
], columns=["Slot", "id", "#par", "Response-surface character", "Recommendation"])
A
```

Additional notes for a10: (i) every slot's parameters are bounded and the box is rectangular by
construction (the HBV ordering and all integer parameters are handled *inside* the models); (ii) a02 warns
that the NSE/KGE surface is dominated by a handful of flood years (WY1961, WY1974, WY1980), so multi-start
and a seeded, reproducible search are essential; (iii) the internal train/validation split
(1952-10-01…1981-09-30 / 1981-10-01…1988-09-30) is available through
`src.common.data.internal_mask` and must be used for any early stopping or hyperparameter choice.

## Evaluator a16

The five slots plus the five ensembles of @sec-ensembles are the complete list of things to score. Report
KGE and NSE only, with the KGE decomposition ($r$, $\alpha$, $\beta$) as supporting detail, and test the
hypotheses of @sec-hypotheses explicitly. Remember that all models see only 92 warm-up days in the
evaluation window while SAC-SMA's primary store has $\tau\approx250$ d — the initial-state rule of each
slot (all parameter-derived, listed above) is part of the model and must not be re-tuned.

# Decisions recorded {#sec-decisions}

1. **HYMOD replaced by HBV-light** (override of the skill's default portfolio) — justified in @sec-why by
   the non-linear recession ($b = 1.68$), the two-time-scale evidence, the complexity-gradient gap and the
   at-gauge NSE 0.819; the Leaf River historical lineage is preserved by SAC-SMA.
2. **No hybrid slot; hybrids enter as pre-declared ensembles** — implementation risk of a differentiable
   hybrid versus an equivalent scientific question answerable by `ens_physics_plus_ml`.
3. **All initial states are parameter-derived, never observation-derived**, so the same rule applies in
   calibration and evaluation (only 92 warm-up days exist there).
4. **Trainable slots (1, 5) fit coefficients/weights on the internal train window and select
   hyperparameters on the internal validation window**; slot 1 then refits its closed-form coefficients on
   the full calibration metric window, slot 5 does not refit (early stopping needs the held-out window).
5. **Scaling constants are frozen** at the a02 calibration-window values listed in
   `config/models.yaml → scaling:`.
6. **`PFREE` bound widened to 0–0.6** and **`PCTIM` narrowed to 0–0.05** relative to the DREAM Ex. 23 set
   quoted by a01 (measured impervious cover 0.41 %).
